summary: Automatic short-video maker: type a topic and it writes the script, makes AI images or clips, adds voice-over and music, and renders the video.

heroCommands.command: Download the all-in-one package and run start.bat

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Pixelle-Video is an AI engine for short videos. From one topic it writes the narration, generates images or video clips for each sentence, synthesizes the voice, adds background music and assembles the final video, all from a web interface.
sixtySeconds.problem: Making a short explainer or social video takes scripting, visuals, voice recording and editing. Pixelle-Video does all of it from a single topic, with no editing experience needed.
whoFor: ComfyUI users who want an automatic pipeline
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a full topic-to-video pipeline with a choice of models: GPT, Qwen, DeepSeek or Ollama for scripts, ComfyUI, RunningHub or direct APIs for visuals, and Edge-TTS or Index-TTS for voice.
requirements: An LLM API key, plus an image/video source (ComfyUI, RunningHub or an API provider)

overview: Windows users can download an all-in-one package that includes Python, uv and ffmpeg, then double-click start.bat. On macOS and Linux, install uv and ffmpeg, clone the project and start the Streamlit web app with uv.

On first use, open System Configuration and set the LLM (preset models fill the base URL for you), then either a ComfyUI/RunningHub setup or direct API media providers such as OpenAI, DashScope, Seedream/Seedance or Kling.
The interface has three columns: content input, voice and visual settings, and generation. It supports portrait and landscape formats and several templates. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Needs API keys or a local ComfyUI
Quality depends on the models you configure

steps.title: Download and extract
steps.body: Get the latest Windows All-in-One Package from the Releases page.

steps.title: Start
steps.body: Double-click start.bat; the browser opens http://localhost:8501.

steps.title: Configure
steps.body: Set your LLM API and image generation service in System Configuration.

steps.title: Install uv
steps.body: Follow the uv installation guide, then check with uv --version.

steps.title: Install ffmpeg (macOS)
steps.body: On Ubuntu/Debian use sudo apt update && sudo apt install ffmpeg.

firstRun.title: Configure models
firstRun.body: Expand System Configuration, pick an LLM preset and enter its key, then set up ComfyUI, RunningHub or an API media provider. Click Save Configuration.

firstRun.title: Enter a topic
firstRun.body: Type a topic in the left column.

tutorial.title: Make your first short video

steps.title: Choose voice and visuals
steps.body: Pick a TTS voice, a visual style and the video size.

steps.title: Generate
steps.body: Click generate in the right column and wait for rendering.

tutorial.expected: A narrated video with AI visuals and background music.

costs.label: Pixelle-Video
costs.value: Free and open source under Apache 2.0.

costs.label: LLM and media APIs
costs.value: Billed by the providers you configure; local ComfyUI or Ollama can avoid API costs.

troubleshooting.solution: Check ffmpeg -version works in your terminal.
Test the ComfyUI connection or check the provider key in System Configuration.
